comments.text: I have a comment about the tipping part. I remember back about 20+ years ago tipping with something a complementary because a customer wanted to bless the other person. But now there’s some restaurants I’ve experienced they force you to tip or else you cannot process your order. I typically tip not because somebody is super busy. I tip on their performance and interaction with me. I found some waitresses or waiters. Don’t really check how the mail is going if there’s anything else I needed at the table or asking if I need a refill of a drink just very common sense management that should be applied during training. So when I do see poor management, I don’t tip hardly anything, especially if the server was being rude. But if I do sometimes tip I try to minimum do $20 when I can afford that extra to bless them. But with everything going on economy wise and trying to find a job that able to provide this extra expenses, it’s gonna be more challenging. But also with the tipping if I may finally say that the businesses need to pay at least $15+ period and I just expect the clients to pay their wages. I think that’s another thing is that when the companies do not value their employees then employees don’t put a lot of effort because they don’t get much out of it.
